ai.literal: without speaking by looking intention he who knows always unchanging water to the world ornament
ai.translation: He who knows another's intention just by looking, without a word being spoken, is an everlasting ornament to this world surrounded by the unceasing sea.
ai.modern: ஒருவர் வாய்திறந்து சொல்லாமலேயே, அவரது முகத்தை நோக்கி அவரது குறிப்பை அறியும் ஆற்றல் உடையவன், வற்றாத கடலால் சூழப்பட்ட இந்த உலகத்திற்கு எப்போதும் ஒரு அணிகலன் ஆவான்.
ai.explanation: This couplet praises the rare ability to read minds. A person who can understand what another is thinking merely by looking at them, without needing any words to be spoken, possesses a profound skill. The poet describes such a person as a permanent jewel to the earth, which is bounded by the ever-present ocean. The phrase 'māṟā nīr' refers to the unchanging, unceasing waters of the sea that surround the world, emphasizing the enduring value of such an insightful person.

ai.literal: Without doubting, that which is inside, him who understands, with a god equally consider.
ai.translation: Consider the one who unerringly understands what is in another's mind to be equal to a god.
ai.modern: பிறர் மனத்திற்குள் இருப்பதைச் சிறிதும் ஐயமில்லாமல் சரியாக உணர்ந்து கொள்பவரைத் தெய்வத்திற்குச் சமமாக மதிக்க வேண்டும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights the extraordinary ability to read another person's mind. The word 'ஐயப்படாஅது' means doing so unerringly, without any doubt or hesitation. 'அகத்தது' refers to the unexpressed thoughts hidden inside the mind. Because perceiving the unseen is a superhuman trait, the text advises that a person who possesses this profound intuition should be regarded as equal to a god.

ai.literal: By indication, intention those who understand, among limbs whatever even having given, one should secure.
ai.translation: Secure the service of those who can read another's intention through mere indication, even if it means giving up any of your own limbs or possessions.
ai.modern: ஒருவருடைய முகக் குறிப்பைக் கொண்டே அவருடைய உள்ளக் குறிப்பை அறியும் ஆற்றல் உடையவரை, தம்முடைய உறுப்புகளுள் எதைக் கொடுத்தாவது தமக்குத் துணையாகச் சேர்த்துக் கொள்ள வேண்டும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet emphasizes the immense value of people who can read minds through subtle non-verbal cues. The phrase 'குறிப்பின் குறிப்பு உணர்வாரை' refers to those who can deduce another's hidden intention simply by observing their outward indications. To secure such a person's service, the text advises giving up 'உறுப்பினுள் யாது' (whatever among one's limbs or possessions). Here, 'உறுப்பு' can mean a physical limb or a vital part of one's wealth, serving as a hyperbole to show that no price is too high for such an advisor.

ai.literal: What was intended / without saying / with those who grasp / others / limbs / one / they are like / indeed / different.
ai.translation: Those who grasp what is intended without it being spoken, and those who cannot, may look alike in their physical limbs, but they are entirely different.
ai.modern: சொல்லாமலேயே குறிப்பினை அறிந்து கொள்பவர்களோடு மற்றவர்கள் உறுப்புகளால் ஒரே மாதிரியாக இருந்தாலும், அறிவால் முற்றிலும் வேறுபட்டவர்கள் ஆவர்.
ai.explanation: This couplet contrasts those who can read intentions without words and those who cannot. The phrase 'குறித்தது கூறாமைக் கொள்வார்' refers to people who intuitively grasp what is in another's mind. The word 'ஏனை' refers to the others who lack this ability. Though both groups share the same physical form ('உறுப்பு ஓர் அனையர்'), the poet declares they are fundamentally different ('வேறு') in their inner capacity.

ai.literal: By intention intention perceive-not if, among organs what yielding [are] eyes?
ai.translation: If they cannot perceive another's intention through their own, what use are the eyes among the body's organs?
ai.modern: ஒருவருடைய முகக் குறிப்பைக் கொண்டு அவருடைய உள்ளக் குறிப்பை அறிய முடியாவிட்டால், உடலில் உள்ள உறுப்புகளில் கண்களால் என்ன பயன்?
ai.explanation: This couplet questions the true purpose of sight if it lacks insight. The word 'குறிப்பு' (intention or sign) appears twice, contrasting the observer's perceptive focus with the unspoken thoughts of the other person. If the eyes cannot read these subtle signs, they are merely physical organs that yield no real benefit.

ai.literal: What is near will show crystal like; mind what is felt will show face.
ai.translation: Just as a crystal reflects the color of whatever is near it, the face reflects the emotions harbored in the mind.
ai.modern: தன்னை அடுத்துள்ள பொருளின் நிறத்தைக் காட்டும் பளிங்கைப் போல, ஒருவருடைய நெஞ்சத்தில் உள்ள உணர்வை அவருடைய முகம் காட்டிவிடும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet uses a simple simile to explain how inner thoughts are revealed outwardly. A clear crystal naturally takes on and reflects the color of any object placed next to it. In the exact same way, a person's face acts as a mirror for their mind. The word 'kaṭuttatu' can mean anger, but in this chapter about reading intentions, it refers broadly to any strong emotion or thought harbored inside. Whatever is deeply felt in the heart is unmistakably displayed on the face.

ai.translation: Is there anything more perceptive than the face? Whether the mind feels joy or anger, the face shows it first.
ai.modern: ஒருவர் மகிழ்ந்தாலும் கோபப்பட்டாலும், அதை அவருக்கு முன்பாகவே அவரது முகம் காட்டிவிடும். எனவே முகத்தை விட அறிவுடையது வேறு எதுவும் இல்லை.
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights the face as the ultimate mirror of the mind. The word 'mutukkuṟaintatu' refers to mature wisdom or sharp intelligence, attributing a perceptive quality to the face. Because the face instantly reveals inner feelings like joy or anger before the person even speaks, it is considered the most intelligent part of the body.

ai.explanation: This couplet highlights the value of companions who can read one's mind. It is entirely sufficient to simply stand before them and look at their face, as they will instantly grasp what needs to be done.

ai.literal: Enmity and friendship the eye will tell, of the eye the variety those who understand if obtained.
ai.translation: The eye will reveal both enmity and friendship, if one secures the help of those who understand its varied expressions.
ai.modern: கண்களின் குறிப்புகளை அறியும் ஆற்றல் உடையவர்களைத் துணையாகப் பெற்றால், ஒருவரின் பகைமையையும் நட்பையும் அவர் கண்களே காட்டிக் கொடுத்துவிடும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights the communicative power of the eyes in revealing a person's true feelings. The words pagaimaiyum and kenmaiyum represent the two extremes of human relationships: enmity and friendship. The phrase kannin vagaimai refers to the subtle varieties of expressions the eye can take. If a leader secures the counsel of those who can read these expressions, as indicated by unarvar perin, the eyes of others will openly declare their hidden intentions.

ai.translation: When you look for the measuring rod of those who say "we are sharp," it is nothing other than the eye.
ai.modern: 'நாங்கள் நுண்ணறிவு உடையவர்கள்' என்று கூறுபவர்களின் அளவுகோலை ஆராய்ந்து பார்த்தால், அது மற்றவர்களின் கண்களைத் தவிர வேறு எதுவும் இல்லை.
ai.explanation: This couplet reveals the secret tool of those who are skilled at reading minds. People who claim to have the subtle intelligence to understand unspoken thoughts rely entirely on observing others. When we look for their measuring rod, we find it is nothing other than the eyes of the people they interact with. The eyes serve as a precise instrument that measures and reveals a person's true inner feelings.
